# Running the notebooks {#sec-running}

## Three ways to use this companion

1. **Read the website.** The live panels run in the browser with no installation.
2. **Run the code in Google Colab.** Every chapter starts with an **Open in Colab** button. Colab is free and runs in the browser;
   you only need a Google account. Use *File → Save a copy in Drive* to keep your changes.
3. **Run it on your computer** with Jupyter, or rebuild the whole book with Quarto.

## Installation

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt     # numpy scipy matplotlib pandas jupyter ipywidgets (+ optional colour-science)
quarto preview                      # live preview while editing
quarto render                       # builds _book/ (HTML)
```

Rendering executes every Python cell once. Results are cached in `_freeze/` (`freeze: auto`), so later builds only re-run the
chapters you changed.

## Publishing the website (GitHub Pages)

The source lives at <https://github.com/{{< var github_user >}}/{{< var repo >}}> (folder `{{< var subdir >}}/`) and the site at
<https://{{< var github_user >}}.github.io/{{< var repo >}}/{{< var subdir >}}/>. After editing a chapter:

```bash
cd notebooks && python build_notebooks.py && cd ..         # refresh the notebooks (Colab buttons point to them)
git add -A && git commit -m "Update chapter 3" && git push   # update the source on GitHub
bash ../publish.sh                                         # render and update the website
```

## Regenerating the notebooks

```bash
cd notebooks
python build_notebooks.py
```

The script converts every chapter, adds a setup cell that works both locally and in Colab (it downloads `semilib.py` from
GitHub when running in Colab), and rebuilds `interactive_explorers.ipynb`.

## The `semilib` module

| function | purpose |
|---|---|
| `kT`, `photon_energy_eV`, `wavelength_from_eV`, `CM3`, `CM2` | units and conversions (SI inside, eV for energies) |
| `MATERIALS`, `VARSHNI`, `varshni`, `LATTICE`, `vegard`, `alloy_Eg` | material data (Table 3.1), bandgap vs temperature and composition |
| `dos_3d`, `fermi_dirac`, `fermi_half`, `eff_dos`, `n_i` | band statistics |
| `carriers`, `fermi_level`, `conductivity`, `einstein_D` | doping, Fermi level, transport |
| `built_in_voltage`, `depletion`, `junction_profile` | pn junction electrostatics |
| `diode_currents`, `diode_iv_rs` | diffusion, recombination and generation currents; series resistance |
| `c_dep`, `r_d`, `c_diff` | small-signal model |
| `led_spectrum`, `led_linewidth`, `wavelength_rgb` | LED emission spectrum |
| `qw_infinite`, `qw_finite`, `qw_wavefunction` | quantum wells |
| `extraction_ratio`, `V_photopic`, `luminous_flux` | extraction efficiency and photometry |
| `led_response`, `led_pulse` | modulation bandwidth and pulse response |

Every function was checked against the worked examples of the slides (see the "worked example" sections).
